Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

Film Club

Membership information

  • The club meets every 2 weeks.
  • No (1)_____ limit.
  • Student membership costs £ (2)_____ per season.

Members get:

  • Free entry to club films.
  • £ (3)_____ reduction on other films at the cinema.
  • Members are entitled to 3 hours' free (4)_____.

Films to be shown:

Oct 14: Pablo

  • About a child in (5)_____ who’s run away from home and wins a (6)_____ competition on TV.

Oct 28: The Soldier

  • With live (7)_____ accompaniment.
  • Made in the year (8)_____.
  • Type of film: a (9)_____.

Nov 11: Tiger

  • Cartoon aimed at adults.
  • Followed by a (10)_____ given by the director.

parts.transcript: Thank you for coming to today's meeting, everyone. I'd like to give you some information about moving to our new office building so that you know what the plans are. As you know, you can't open the windows in this building, but I suggest you use the gloves that we'll provide. I'll start with the benefits. Using briquettes has a financial benefit because they make use of waste products as raw materials, so there isn't any cost involved for that. Another advantage is convenience. Handling briquettes is cleaner than handling materials like wood or charcoal. Also, briquettes are less trouble to store because they're a uniform size and shape. Right, let's look briefly now at how these briquettes are made. There are two basic methods of manufacture. The first method uses machinery. At the initial stage, all the loose plant material is ground into a powder and then mixed with other materials. Next, a machine compresses the biomass mixture, and that process raises the temperature and causes it to melt. The machine forces the biomass mixture out through rectangular or circular holes. Then, as the pressure decreases, the mixture cools and becomes solid again, and that's how the briquettes are formed. It's important to point out that with this method, electricity is essential to operate the machinery, and the exact amount you need depends on the type of biomass you use. But generally, the amount required is only 3% to 9% of the energy that's produced by the briquettes when they are burnt. The second method involves making briquettes by hand. This method is suitable when the biomass is mainly composed of material that doesn't melt, like paper. The biomass is made into a paste by adding water and, in addition, something sticky, such as starch. This mixture is then shaped using either a simple metal press or bare hands. So, where is biomass fuel used, and how extensively? passages.passageHtml:
Fantastic cycling trails

A. Kirkstone Water to Ravenscraig Castle, Dundee

Enjoy a relaxed ride from Kirkstone Water to the impressive Ravenscraig Castle along a route that remains almost entirely flat. Along the way, you will pass several notable sights, including striking views of three bridges crossing the River Tay. Once you reach the castle, either retrace your route or continue towards Broughty Ferry for a longer adventure.

B. The Ashford Canal Cycle Path, Cornwall

Follow the peaceful Ashford Canal and keep watch for dragonflies, swans, buzzards, fish and other local wildlife. The well-maintained path is broad enough for families to cycle together safely and comfortably. For an added cultural stop, take a short detour to explore the gardens and historic surroundings of the 13th-century Trelowen Castle.

C. Alder Brook Walking and Cycling Path, Manchester

Escape the noise of Manchester on this surprisingly tranquil route beside the Alder Brook. The path is mostly level and suitable for several types of bicycle, although riders are advised to walk across the single hump-backed bridge. Follow the signs for another two kilometres to Hollybank Valley Country Park, where you can enjoy a picnic and visit a popular family attraction famous for its sheep.

D. Kielder Forest Cycle Trail, Northumberland

Discover the heritage of Northumberland on a trail following a former railway line once used during the region’s coal-mining era. Historical landmarks, beautiful woodland scenery and numerous picnic areas make the journey both fascinating and relaxing. The route is circular, clearly signposted and suitable for families, while dogs are also welcome to join the adventure.

E. The Solway Trail, Carlisle

The Solway Trail offers safe, level cycling with plenty of cafés available whenever you need a break. Enjoy sweeping views towards southern Scotland and have a rest on the beach at Allonby or Silloth. More ambitious cyclists can continue towards Gretna, with direct train services from either Wigton or Gretna providing a convenient return journey to Carlisle.

passages.title: Section 2: The Sunflower Training Institute
passages.passageHtml:
The Sunflower Training Institute

Welcome

Welcome to The Sunflower Training Institute. We are delighted that you have chosen to study with us. This booklet introduces the Institute and outlines the key features, facilities and regulations associated with our programmes.

Courses

The Sunflower was established to provide high-quality, short-term professional training across a broad range of career fields. Our teaching staff are exceptionally well qualified, and all have gained teaching experience abroad at some point in their careers.

Programmes at The Sunflower are divided into modules. Most modules last ten weeks, although some are shorter. The majority of programmes, including Office Management, Librarianship and Medical Records Organisation, consist of two modules. Others, such as Biotechnology and Computer Analysis, comprise three or four modules.

There is a two-week break between modules. As no coursework or assignments are due during these periods, students are encouraged to take a holiday and return refreshed for the next stage of their programme.

Class hours vary according to the requirements of each programme and are therefore not standardised across the Institute. Students should consult the timetable printed at the beginning of their course handbook.

The Sunflower cannot award attendance or achievement certificates to students who miss parts of their programme because they have failed to check their timetable carefully. However, genuine reasons for absence, such as illness, will be considered when appropriate supporting documentation is provided.

Students may still qualify for an attendance certificate and, subject to meeting the relevant academic requirements, an achievement certificate if they have attended at least 80 per cent of their scheduled classes and submit a medical certificate covering the period of absence.

Facilities

The opening hours of the snack bar, coffee lounge and restaurant are listed below your course timetable. Please note that the coffee lounge is closed after 4 p.m.

Reservations are not required at any of the Institute’s dining facilities, except at the restaurant on Friday and Saturday evenings.

The coffee lounge and restaurant are normally closed on public holidays. However, groups of twenty or more may reserve the restaurant for dinner on these days. A non-refundable deposit is required when making a booking.

The Institute also has an excellent sports complex. The swimming pool is open daily from 8.00 am to 8.00 pm and is reserved exclusively free of charge to Sunflower students who present a valid enrolment card. Students with a valid enrolment card may reserve a squash court for $4.50 per half-hour. Gymnasium access is available under the following payment options:

passages.title: Section 3: Starting school later has positive effects on teens
passages.passageHtml:
Starting school later has positive effects on teens

A growing body of evidence demonstrates that adolescents benefit substantially from additional sleep. When school districts postpone the start of the academic day, measurable improvements tend to follow. With lessons that commence as early as 7 a.m. and buses that arrive well before sunrise, roughly 80 per cent of US children in grades 6 through 12 fail to obtain the recommended quantity of sleep during term time, according to research by the National Sleep Foundation, a sleep advocacy organisation. These premature start times appear to contribute to a multitude of difficulties. Exhausted children, studies indicate, not only struggle with irritability, but also with symptoms of depression. They tend to gain weight, their academic grades deteriorate, and many resort to caffeine, with dubious consequences for productivity and uncertain effects upon the development of immature brains.

Now, propelled by accumulating research suggesting that adolescents are biologically predisposed to sleep late, and that delaying school start times by even a mere 30 minutes generates a pronounced difference in how well teenagers feel and perform, an increasing number of institutions across the United States are beginning the school day later than they formerly did. Many more are deliberating the question. Simultaneously, however, there remain entrenched pockets of resistance from administrators and parents who contend that bus schedules will become excessively complicated, that a later commencement will interfere with extracurricular programmes, or that children will simply remain awake later if they realise they can sleep in somewhat longer.

According to Kyla Wahlstrom, director of the Center for Applied Research and Educational Improvement at the University of Minnesota, although the two districts she examined could not have been more different in terms of race, socioeconomic status and other factors, beneficial changes in both places became apparent almost immediately.

Several of the outcomes were notably significant. For instance, students were perceptibly more alert during the first two periods of the day. Furthermore, the cafeteria was calmer, and fewer altercations erupted in the corridors. Students, who were now obtaining nearly an additional hour of sleep each night, reported that they felt less depressed. Even parents informed teachers that they considered their children easier to live with than before.

The melatonin shift

Biology, rather than laziness, should be held responsible for adolescents’ reluctance to rise in the morning. As children mature and approach puberty, a phase of profound biological transformation, their bodies begin to circulate melatonin—the hormone that induces sleepiness—approximately two hours later than they previously did.

Consequently, teenagers find it virtually impossible to fall asleep before roughly 11 p.m., even when they make a deliberate attempt to retire earlier. Yet adolescents nonetheless require an average of 9.25 hours of slumber each night. Superimposed upon this shift in natural sleeping and waking rhythms lies a second factor: a phase of intense drowsiness that afflicts both adults and adolescents during the early-morning hours. In adults, this trough in alertness occurs between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m.; in adolescents, it descends between approximately 5 a.m. and 7 a.m. The implication is that, while their alarm clocks instruct teenagers to leave their beds and demand that their brains perform, their bodies are simultaneously signalling them to continue sleeping.

Beyond these mood, behavioural and learning consequences, scientists are progressively uncovering more subtle mechanisms through which such chronic sleep deprivation can damage children. Certain studies, for example, demonstrate that insufficient sleep compromises the immune system. Others suggest that, when sleep is inadequate, the body secretes elevated quantities of the hormones that trigger hunger, a process that may plausibly contribute to escalating rates of obesity.

In order to remain awake, young people frequently resort to coffee, soda and other caffeinated beverages. At one public high school in the eastern US state of Massachusetts, 95 per cent of the students surveyed reported consuming caffeine within the preceding fortnight—predominantly in the form of soda rather than coffee, and most commonly during the afternoon and evening hours—Dr Amy Wolfson and a colleague reported in the journal Health Education and Behavior. According to Dr Wolfson, no published guidelines currently specify how much caffeine constitutes an excessive amount for adolescents. The substance, however, persists within the body for up to five hours—three hours longer than was originally assumed—thereby depriving teenagers of an indeterminate number of hours of sleep. Even when caffeinated teenagers do manage to fall asleep, caffeine demonstrably renders the quality of that sleep worse. Finally, no one yet understands how caffeine may influence developing brains, although numerous experts remain concerned about the apparent connection between the sugar contained in soda and consequent weight gain.

Schools respond

As the body of sleep research continues to accumulate, an expanding number of schools are gravitating towards later start times. No one has formally documented precisely how many institutions have implemented the change, yet experts report that they are receiving a steadily increasing volume of enquiries from districts throughout the US, requesting advice on whether and how to adopt a later schedule. Whatever the practical obstacles, adolescents need to obtain sufficient sleep, and altering school start times has proven to be one effective means of achieving that objective.

task1.prompt: You recently stayed at a hotel on an official business trip and encountered several problems during your stay. Write a formal letter to the hotel manager. task1.sampleBand8Answer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to formally register my disappointment regarding the quality of accommodation during my stay at the Grand Imperial Hotel from October 18th to October 21st (Booking Reference: #GI-98421). I was visiting your city as the keynote speaker at the International Energy Symposium.

Regrettably, multiple deficiencies compromised what ought to have been a restful business visit. First, despite confirming a high-floor executive quiet room weeks prior, I was assigned Room 204 adjacent to the main loading dock, where delivery freight commenced noisily at 5:00 AM each morning. Furthermore, the high-speed Wi-Fi connection advertised in the executive suite failed intermittently throughout my stay, preventing me from accessing critical presentation materials for my conference.

To compound these issues, when I raised these urgent concerns with the front desk duty supervisor on the morning of October 19th, the staff member appeared dismissive and failed to offer an alternative room or technical support.

In light of these inconveniences and the substandard service rendered, I request a refund of 50% of the total accommodation fee charged to my corporate card. Additionally, I would appreciate a written assurance detailing the measures you intend to institute to improve staff responsiveness and internet stability.

I look forward to receiving your prompt resolution.

Yours faithfully,
Dr. Jonathan Miller

task2.title: Task 2: General Essay
task2.prompt: In many countries today, people are spending less time with their families and more time at work or pursuing individual hobbies. What are the causes of this trend, and what effects does it have on society?
task2.sampleBand8Answer:
In contemporary society, an increasing number of individuals devote an overwhelming proportion of their daily lives to workplace commitments and autonomous pastimes, resulting in a noticeable decline in familial interaction. This essay will examine the primary catalysts behind this phenomenon and discuss its profound ramifications for community cohesion.

The primary impetus behind diminishing family time is escalating economic pressure and the competitive nature of the globalized job market. With housing costs and general living expenses soaring in metropolitan hubs, adults frequently find themselves obliged to work excessive overtime or manage secondary freelance gigs to attain financial stability. Concurrently, the pervasive presence of personalized digital entertainment—such as algorithmic social media and on-demand streaming—encourages solitary engagement rather than collective domestic pastimes.

Regarding the impacts, this societal transition generates considerable adverse repercussions. Within the household, the lack of parental presence and meaningful communication can weaken intergenerational bonding, leaving children vulnerable to behavioral issues and emotional isolation. At a broader societal level, the erosion of cohesive family structures diminishes the collective resilience of communities, as strong domestic units have traditionally served as the initial safety net during psychological and financial crises.

In summary, intense corporate demands and digital individualism represent the chief reasons why people are drifting from domestic life. Unless societies institute sustainable work-life balance policies, familial ties and social well-being will continue to erode.

I would like to speak about a defining professional achievement from last year, when I successfully spearheaded the migration of our company's legacy customer management infrastructure to a secure cloud platform. This undertaking occurred over a grueling six-month period at our regional corporate headquarters.

The primary obstacle we confronted was the sheer complexity of legacy data formats, compounded by an unforgiving deployment deadline. We had to ensure zero downtime for over fifty thousand active global clients while synchronizing disparate legacy databases. Furthermore, midway through the project, several senior specialists had to quarantine due to seasonal health issues, which forced me to shoulder additional architectural duties and coordinate with offshore teams across multiple time zones.
